methods.label: Express the two voting margins
methods.explanation:
Because exactly \(400\) members vote each time, knowing one side's count determines the other. Let \(u\) be the number originally voting against the bill, and let \(v\) be the number voting for it on the second vote.

The original supporting count is \(400-u\), so the defeat margin is
\[
u-(400-u)=2u-400.
\]
The second opposing count is \(400-v\), so the passage margin is \(2v-400\). The passage margin is twice the defeat margin, giving
\[
2v-400=2(2u-400),
\qquad v=2u-200.
\]
The other condition says \(v=12u/11\). Substituting this into the margin equation gives
\[
\frac{12u}{11}=2u-200,
\]
so \(12u=22u-2200\), and therefore \(u=220\). It follows that \(v=240\), while the original supporting count was \(400-220=180\). These counts give defeat and passage margins of \(40\) and \(80\), respectively, as required.

The increase in support was
\[
240-180=\boxed{60}
\]
members, choice B.
